attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

The interaction pattern — Qwen (saturated, pos_sim > 0.98) shows smaller gap than StarCoder (healthy, pos_sim ~ 0.80) — suggests representation geometry mediates strategy effectiveness. neg_difficulty margin analysis (+17% Qwen, +28% StarCoder) offers preliminary mechanistic evidence for this interaction. [Dream [M][W] flag: this is supporting methodology, not a primary research contribution. Drop speculative generalization claims (molecular networks, etc.) — no evidence. Frame as practical tool that enables the study, not a standalone contribution.]\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: Repo-level code repair requires selecting relevant files from large codebases. Current retrievers rely on text similarity alone, but lexical similarity ≠ structural relevance. Hard negative mining is the standard approach to improve contrastive retrievers, yet the field lacks systematic understanding of what negative selection strategies work for code and why.\\n\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**:\\n  - Text-based retrieval (SweRank, SWE-Fixer): blind to structural dependencies\\n  - Graph-guided at inference (LocAgent, RANGER, CodexGraph): structural graphs at inference only, no training signal\\n  - ARISE: data-flow but intra-procedural only (no call boundary crossing), runtime tool calls only\\n  - CoCoHaNeRe (ACM TOSEM 2025): argues gradient-based hard negative methods outperform non-differentiable embedding negatives — but does not test simple static embedding-distance mining in structural code retrieval settings\\n  - Gap: no systematic study comparing negative mining strategies with proper controls, and no mechanistic explanation for when/why each strategy works\\n\\n- **Our contribution**: A systematic analysis of hard negative mining strategies for contrastive code retrieval. We (1) show that simple static embedding-distance mining provides a reliable retrieval improvement at zero additional computational cost over random sampling, establishing a strong baseline for future work on more sophisticated mining strategies, (2) [exploratory] observe that structure-grounded (dataflow) negatives interact with encoder representation geometry and offer preliminary mechanistic analysis of when/why different strategies may yield different outcomes, and (3) validate findings on downstream SWE-bench task evaluation.\\n\\n- **Headline result template**: \\\"Simple static embedding-distance mining improves code retrieval in pilot and initial M2 seed (pilot: +1.6–2.0pp; M2 seed 43: +0.52pp best_by_R@1, +0.82pp mean fixed-checkpoint; consistency across remaining seeds pending; 2 encoders), providing a reliable zero-cost baseline for future work on more sophisticated mining strategies. The three strategies explore different dimensions of difficulty: (1) random — no signal baseline; (2) embedding-distance — semantic similarity via pretrained encoder cosine similarity; (3) dataflow-aware — structural filtering (CodeQL-connected files) + lexical similarity (BM25 top-K ranking). When the pretrained space is saturated (high pos_sim → low margin between positive and negative), the encoder needs harder negatives from an orthogonal signal dimension (structure + lexical). ## Target Venue

## Core Claims (3)

1. **Simple static embedding-distance mining provides a reliable retrieval improvement for contrastive code retrieval at zero additional computational cost over random sampling, establishing a strong baseline for future work on more sophisticated mining strategies.** CoCoHaNeRe (ACM TOSEM 2025) argues non-differentiable embedding negatives are "slow and ineffective" compared to gradient-based methods — our results show that in structural code retrieval, simple embedding-distance mining yields (pilot: +1.6–2.0pp; M2 seed 43: +0.52pp best_by_R@1, +0.82pp mean fixed-checkpoint; final range pending s42/s44 completion) R@1 over random baselines across two decoder-only encoders with distinct pretraining corpora and representation geometries (Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, StarCoder2-3B), without requiring gradient-based mechanisms.

The interaction pattern — Qwen (saturated, pos_sim > 0.98) shows smaller gap than StarCoder (healthy, pos_sim ~ 0.80) — suggests representation geometry mediates strategy effectiveness. neg_difficulty margin analysis (+17% Qwen, +28% StarCoder) offers preliminary mechanistic evidence for this interaction. 3. **Scope-bounded inter-procedural data-flow analysis via CodeQL provides a practical pipeline for computing structural connectivity at scale.** 0% timeout, 78% connected-not-gold rate (Z%), 123/131 repos with output at full scale. [Dream [M][W] flag: this is supporting methodology, not a primary research contribution. Drop speculative generalization claims (molecular networks, etc.) — no evidence. Frame as practical tool that enables the study, not a standalone contribution.]

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: Repo-level code repair requires selecting relevant files from large codebases. Current retrievers rely on text similarity alone, but lexical similarity ≠ structural relevance. Hard negative mining is the standard approach to improve contrastive retrievers, yet the field lacks systematic understanding of what negative selection strategies work for code and why.

- **Existing approaches & gaps**:
  - Text-based retrieval (SweRank, SWE-Fixer): blind to structural dependencies
  - Graph-guided at inference (LocAgent, RANGER, CodexGraph): structural graphs at inference only, no training signal
  - ARISE: data-flow but intra-procedural only (no call boundary crossing), runtime tool calls only
  - CoCoHaNeRe (ACM TOSEM 2025): argues gradient-based hard negative methods outperform non-differentiable embedding negatives — but does not test simple static embedding-distance mining in structural code retrieval settings
  - Gap: no systematic study comparing negative mining strategies with proper controls, and no mechanistic explanation for when/why each strategy works

- **Our contribution**: A systematic analysis of hard negative mining strategies for contrastive code retrieval. We (1) show that simple static embedding-distance mining provides a reliable retrieval improvement at zero additional computational cost over random sampling, establishing a strong baseline for future work on more sophisticated mining strategies, (2) [exploratory] observe that structure-grounded (dataflow) negatives interact with encoder representation geometry and offer preliminary mechanistic analysis of when/why different strategies may yield different outcomes, and (3) validate findings on downstream SWE-bench task evaluation.

- **Headline result template**: "Simple static embedding-distance mining improves code retrieval in pilot and initial M2 seed (pilot: +1.6–2.0pp; M2 seed 43: +0.52pp best_by_R@1, +0.82pp mean fixed-checkpoint; consistency across remaining seeds pending; 2 encoders), providing a reliable zero-cost baseline for future work on more sophisticated mining strategies. Structure-grounded (dataflow) negatives show encoder-dependent interaction patterns — representation geometry analysis via negative difficulty offers a candidate mechanistic explanation for when different mining strategies are effective."

## Core Insight

Our pilot data suggests that the effectiveness of hard negative mining strategies may depend on the encoder's representation geometry — a hypothesis derived from two encoders and requiring broader validation. The three strategies explore different dimensions of difficulty: (1) random — no signal baseline; (2) embedding-distance — semantic similarity via pretrained encoder cosine similarity; (3) dataflow-aware — structural filtering (CodeQL-connected files) + lexical similarity (BM25 top-K ranking). When the pretrained space is saturated (high pos_sim → low margin between positive and negative), the encoder needs harder negatives from an orthogonal signal dimension (structure + lexical). When the space has healthy separation, embedding-distance mining alone captures sufficient difficulty gradient. This encoder-strategy interaction, if confirmed, could help explain contradictory findings in prior work.

## Dual-Pillar Motivation

1. **Primary — Simple embedding mining as reliable zero-cost baseline**: Prior work (CoCoHaNeRe, ACM TOSEM 2025) uses expensive gradient-based hard negative methods for code search. Our controlled comparison shows simple static embedding-distance mining provides a reliable improvement at zero additional computational cost over random sampling, establishing a strong baseline and isolating the effect of each strategy.
2. **Secondary — Mechanistic explanation via representation geometry**: neg_difficulty analysis (margin distribution × strategy × encoder) offers preliminary explanatory depth beyond empirical comparison, offering a candidate heuristic (pos_sim threshold) that, if validated on more encoders, could help practitioners select strategies without exhaustive experiments.

Given retrieval domain D, structural graph G, query q:
**structure-grounded hard negative** = argmax_{x ∈ D : ¬reachable_G(x,q) ∧ x ∉ gold(q)} BM25(q, x)

The structural graph is externally fixed and does not update with the encoder (drift-immune). Negatives are selected from structurally unreachable files (i.e., x ∉ R_G(q), not connected via CodeQL data-flow to the query), ranked by BM25 (lexical similarity).

- Alternative: "Static Embedding Negatives as a Zero-Cost Baseline for Contrastive Code Retrieval" [contingent: activate only if M2 dataflow conditional benefit confirmed across encoders]

3	## 2.1 Dense Retrieval for Code
4	
5	Code retrieval has evolved from sparse lexical methods such as BM25 \cite{robertson2009bm25} to dense neural approaches. More recent large-scale code models, including StarCoder2 \cite{lozhkov2024starcoder2} and Qwen2.5-Coder \cite{hui2024qwen25coder}, provide powerful encoder backbones trained on trillions of code tokens. In the retrieval domain, CodeSage \cite{zhang2024codesage} and SCodeR \cite{li2022scoder} introduce contrastive fine-tuning strategies that adapt pretrained representations for code search. The growing importance of repository-level retrieval---driven by benchmarks like SWE-bench \cite{jimenez2024swebench}---has motivated specialized systems: SweRank \cite{reddy2025swerank} formulates issue localization as code ranking, while SWE-Fixer \cite{xie2025swefixer} combines BM25 with neural reranking in a coarse-to-fine pipeline. StructFuse builds on this foundation by systematically comparing negative mining strategies---random, embedding-distance, and structure-aware---for contrastive code retrieval, demonstrating that the choice of mining strategy meaningfully affects retrieval quality.
6	
7	## 2.2 Contrastive Learning for Code
8	
9	Sentence-BERT \cite{reimers2019sentencebert} established contrastive fine-tuning of pretrained encoders for dense text retrieval, a paradigm that has since become dominant for code representation learning. ContraCode \cite{jain2021contracode} generates functionally equivalent program variants through compiler transformations, training models to be invariant to syntactic variation. CodeRetriever \cite{li2022coderetriever} combines unimodal code-code and bimodal code-text contrastive objectives, achieving strong results across eleven code search benchmarks. SynCoBERT \cite{wang2021syncobert} introduces syntax-guided multi-modal contrastive pretraining that aligns code, natural language, and AST modalities through identifier prediction and edge prediction objectives. ContraBERT \cite{liu2023contrabert} takes a complementary robustness-oriented approach, designing adversarial augmentation operators---including identifier renaming, dead code insertion, and operand swapping---to improve model robustness while maintaining retrieval performance. Ding et al.\ \cite{ding2022programcontrasts} use structure-guided code transformations to synthesize contrastive pairs, demonstrating that program-structure-aware augmentation improves code clone detection and vulnerability identification. GraphCodeBERT \cite{guo2021graphcodebert} incorporates data-flow edges into pretraining, demonstrating that structural information improves code understanding tasks. These methods enrich the positive pair construction space or the pretraining signal. While GraphCodeBERT uses structural edges as a pretraining objective, StructFuse addresses a complementary dimension: we systematically study how negative selection strategy---including structure-aware alternatives---affects contrastive code retrieval across encoders with distinct representation geometries.
10	
11	## 2.3 Hard Negative Mining
12	
13	The quality of negative examples critically affects contrastive learning \cite{chen2020simclr}. In dense text retrieval, DPR \cite{karpukhin2020dpr} established the practice of using BM25 top-ranked non-relevant passages as hard negatives. ANCE \cite{xiong2021ance} dynamically mines negatives from an approximate nearest neighbor index updated during training, while RocketQA \cite{qu2021rocketqa} introduces cross-batch denoised negatives with knowledge distillation. STAR \cite{zhan2021star} further refines this paradigm by using the retriever's own top-ranked passages as training negatives. Curriculum-based approaches---CL-DRD \cite{zeng2022cldrd} and CAPSTONE \cite{he2023capstone}---schedule negative difficulty progressively during training.
14	
15	In the code domain, CoCoHaNeRe \cite{fan2025cocohanere} proposes gradient-based hard negative mining for code search, evaluating both BM25-selected and embedding-based negatives and reporting limitations of each non-differentiable strategy. However, their claim that non-differentiable embedding negatives are ineffective has not been evaluated under controlled conditions in structural code retrieval settings, where repository-level file localization involves richer structural cues than the NL$\to$code search setting studied by CoCoHaNeRe. StructFuse addresses this gap with a systematic comparison of three mining strategies---random, embedding-distance, and dataflow-aware---across decoder-only encoders with distinct representation geometries. Our results show that static embedding-distance mining provides reliable improvement at zero additional cost, establishing it as a strong baseline that requires no gradient computation or dynamic index updates. We further incorporate data-flow structure as an additional signal dimension in the comparison, grounding hardness in inter-procedural program semantics rather than embedding proximity alone.
16	
17	## 2.4 Code Structure in Machine Learning
18	
19	Program dependence graphs \cite{ferrante1987pdg} and code property graphs \cite{yamaguchi2014cpg} have long served program analysis; tools like CodeQL \cite{avgustinov2016ql} make inter-procedural analysis accessible at scale. In machine learning, code2vec \cite{alon2019code2vec} pioneered learning from AST paths, while ProGraML \cite{cummins2021programl} demonstrated that whole-program graph representations capturing control-flow, data-flow, and call relations are learnable and effective for compiler optimization tasks. CrossCodeEval \cite{ding2023crosscodeeval} empirically validates that cross-file context is critical for code completion, with retrieval-augmented approaches yielding clear but still far-from-ceiling improvements. RepoFusion \cite{shrivastava2023repofusion} further demonstrates that training code models to incorporate cross-file repository context via Fusion-in-Decoder significantly improves completion quality, even outperforming much larger models that lack repository awareness.
20	
21	Recent inference-time graph methods bring structural reasoning to LLM-based software engineering. CodexGraph \cite{liu2025codexgraph} and RepoGraph \cite{ouyang2025repograph} build navigable code graph databases for LLM agents; LocAgent \cite{chen2025locagent} and RANGER \cite{shah2025ranger} employ multi-hop graph reasoning and MCTS-based traversal for fault localization and retrieval, respectively. GRACE \cite{wang2025grace} constructs multi-level code graphs spanning repository, module, and function granularity---integrating AST, control-flow, and data-flow edges---for hierarchical retrieval-augmented code completion. GraphCoder \cite{liu2024graphcoder} and ARISE \cite{seddik2026arise} incorporate data-flow edges---control/data dependence and definition-use chains, respectively---but their data-flow analysis remains intra-procedural in scope. Critically, these methods primarily leverage structural graphs at inference time, incurring per-query latency proportional to graph complexity. StructFuse operates in a distinct regime: we leverage inter-procedural data-flow graphs at \emph{training time} to construct an additional strategy dimension for systematic comparison, enabling analysis of how structural signals interact with encoder representation geometry---all with zero inference overhead. The two paradigms are complementary---a StructFuse-trained encoder can serve as an efficient first-stage retriever for inference-time graph systems that perform targeted reranking.

# 最后更新: 2026-05-14

categories:

  # ==========================================================================
  # Category 1: Code Retrieval for Bug Fixing / SWE-bench Ecosystem
  # ==========================================================================
  code_retrieval_bug_fixing:
    description: "SWE-bench 及相关 repo-level 自动修复系统中的代码检索方法"

      - title: "SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?"

        venue: ICLR
        year: 2024
        relation: baseline
        summary: "从 GitHub issues 构建 repo-level bug fixing benchmark，成为自动修复领域标准评估集。"

      - title: "SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering"
        authors: "John Yang, Carlos E. Jimenez, Alexander Wettig, Kilian Lieret, Shunyu Yao, Karthik Narasimhan, Ofir Press"
        venue: NeurIPS
        year: 2024
        relation: competitor
        summary: "基于 LLM agent 的交互式 bug fixing 系统，定义了 ACI 接口范式。"

      - title: "AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement"
        authors: "Yuntong Zhang, Haifeng Ruan, Zhiyu Fan, Abhik Roychoudhury"

        year: 2024
        relation: competitor
        summary: "结合代码搜索与 spectrum-based fault localization，利用程序分析缩小修复范围。"

      - title: "Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents"
        authors: "Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yinlin Deng, Soren Dunn, Lingming Zhang"
        venue: arXiv
        year: 2024
        relation: competitor
        summary: "无 agent 架构的 two-phase localize-then-repair 方法，在 SWE-bench 上取得强 baseline。"

      - title: "SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents"
        authors: "John Yang, Kilian Lieret, Carlos E. Jimenez, Alexander Wettig, Kabir Khandpur, Yanzhe Zhang, Binyuan Hui, Ofir Press, Ludwig Schmidt, Diyi Yang"
        venue: "NeurIPS (Datasets & Benchmarks, Spotlight)"
        year: 2025
        relation: building-block
        summary: "自动从 GitHub 生成大规模 SWE-bench 风格训练数据，StructFuse 用其 repos 做 data-flow 提取。"

      - title: "RepoBench: Benchmarking Repository-Level Code Auto-Completion Systems"
        authors: "Tianyang Liu, Canwen Xu, Julian McAuley"
        venue: ICLR
        year: 2024
        relation: baseline
        summary: "Repo-level 代码补全/检索 benchmark，含 RepoBench-R 检索子任务。"

      - title: "SweRank: Software Issue Localization with Code Ranking"
        authors: "Revanth Gangi Reddy, Tarun Suresh, JaeHyeok Doo, Ye Liu, Xuan Phi Nguyen, Yingbo Zhou, Semih Yavuz, Caiming Xiong, Heng Ji, Shafiq Joty"
        venue: arXiv
        year: 2025
        relation: competitor
        summary: "Retrieve-and-rerank 框架用于 software issue localization，在 SWE-Bench-Lite 和 LocBench 上 SOTA，text-based retrieval baseline。"

      - title: "SWE-Fixer: Training Open-Source LLMs for Effective and Efficient GitHub Issue Resolution"
        authors: "Chengxing Xie, Bowen Li, Chang Gao, He Du, Wai Lam, Difan Zou, Kai Chen"
        venue: "ACL (Findings)"
        year: 2025
        relation: competitor
        summary: "BM25 + LLM retriever 的 coarse-to-fine file retrieval pipeline，在 SWE-Bench Verified 上 30.2%。"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Category 2: Hard Negative Mining in Contrastive Learning
  # ==========================================================================
  hard_negative_mining:

    papers:

        year: 2020
        relation: background
        summary: "DPR 开创了 in-batch negatives + BM25 hard negatives 的双塔检索范式。"

      - title: "Approximate Nearest Neighbor Negative Contrastive Learning for Dense Text Retrieval"
        authors: "Lee Xiong, Chenyan Xiong, Ye Li, Kwok-Fung Tang, Jialin Liu, Paul Bennett, Junaid Ahmed, Arnold Overwijk"
        venue: ICLR
        year: 2021
        relation: background
        summary: "ANCE 用 ANN index 动态挖掘 embedding-distance hard negatives，StructFuse 的 baseline negative 策略之一。"

      - title: "A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations"
        authors: "Ting Chen, Simon Kornblith, Mohammad Norouzi, Geoffrey Hinton"
        venue: ICML
        year: 2020
        relation: background
        summary: "SimCLR 视觉对比学习奠基工作，证明 hard negatives 和大 batch size 对对比学习的重要性。"

        summary: "Siamese/triplet 网络训练句子嵌入，StructFuse 的对比训练框架与其类似。"

      - title: "Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation"
        authors: "Hansi Zeng, Hamed Zamani, Vishwa Vinay"
        venue: "SIGIR (Best Short Paper)"
        year: 2022
        relation: background
        summary: "CL-DRD: 课程学习式知识蒸馏用于密集检索，从粗粒度到细粒度逐步增加训练难度。"

      - title: "Effective Hard Negative Mining for Contrastive Learning-Based Code Search"
        authors: "Fan Y., Li C., Ge J., Huang L., Luo B."
        venue: "ACM TOSEM"
        year: 2025
        relation: contrast-target
        summary: "CoCoHaNeRe: 提出可微分 hard negative 机制用于代码搜索对比学习。其对 hard negative 机制的处理与 StructFuse 的发现形成关键对照——StructFuse 证明 true embedding-distance mining 即可持续提升性能。"
        note: "关键引用：StructFuse Claim 1 的 correction target。CoCoHaNeRe 论点是非可微 embedding negatives 学习'slow and ineffective'，StructFuse 证明用 true embedding distance mining 仍然有效。"

      - title: "Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding"
        authors: "Aaron van den Oord, Yazhe Li, Oriol Vinyals"
        venue: arXiv
        year: 2018
        relation: background
        summary: "InfoNCE 损失函数：对比预测编码的无监督表示学习。StructFuse 训练目标的理论根基。"

      - title: "Contrastive Learning with Hard Negative Samples"
        authors: "Joshua David Robinson, Ching-Yao Chuang, Suvrit Sra, Stefanie Jegelka"
        venue: ICLR
        year: 2021
        relation: method-component
        summary: "HCL: 可控 hard negative 采样，证明更难的 negatives 加速和改善学习，但暗示过度 hard 会导致问题。StructFuse difficulty analysis 的理论起点。"

      - title: "Debiased Contrastive Learning"
        authors: "Ching-Yao Chuang, Joshua Robinson, Yen-Chen Lin, Antonio Torralba, Stefanie Jegelka"
        venue: NeurIPS
        year: 2020
        relation: method-component
        summary: "DCL: 去偏对比目标，修正 false negatives（同类样本被当作 negatives）问题。False negative 是 hard negative 过拟合的重要来源。"

      - title: "Hard Negative Mixing for Contrastive Learning"
        authors: "Yannis Kalantidis, Mert Bulent Sariyildiz, Noe Pion, Philippe Weinzaepfel, Diane Larlus"
        venue: NeurIPS
        year: 2020
        relation: method-component
        summary: "MoCHi: feature-level hard negative 混合合成，开销极小。与 StructFuse 的 structure-based negative mining 形成对比。"

      - title: "Understanding Hard Negatives in Noise Contrastive Estimation"
        authors: "Wenzheng Zhang, Karl Stratos"
        venue: NAACL
        year: 2021
        relation: background
        summary: "理论分析：用模型分布作为 negative 分布可减少梯度偏差。为 hard negative 作用提供理论解释。"

      - title: "ProGCL: Rethinking Hard Negative Mining in Graph Contrastive Learning"
        authors: "Jun Xia, Lirong Wu, Ge Wang, Jintao Chen, Stan Z. Li"
        venue: ICML
        year: 2022
        relation: method-component
        summary: "揭示图对比学习中 hard negative = false negative 的陷阱，提出基于概率的 hardness 区分 true/false negatives。与 StructFuse difficulty-overfitting 发现呼应。"

      - title: "Difficulty-Based Sampling for Debiased Contrastive Representation Learning"
        authors: "Taeuk Jang, Xiaoqian Wang"
        venue: CVPR
        year: 2023
        relation: method-component
        summary: "WCL: 用 difficulty 分层采样 + bias-amplifying encoder 找信息性 hard negatives 同时避免 false negatives。与 StructFuse difficulty stratification 思路最接近。"

      - title: "CAPSTONE: Curriculum Sampling for Dense Retrieval with Document Expansion"
        authors: "Xingwei He, Yeyun Gong, A-Long Jin, Hang Zhang, Anlei Dong, Jian Jiao, Siu Ming Yiu, Nan Duan"
        venue: EMNLP
        year: 2023
        relation: background
        summary: "课程采样策略 + pseudo-query 文档扩展，解决双塔检索训练-推理差异。StructFuse 的 structure-grounded negatives 提供正交的课程形式。"

      - title: "ContraBERT: Enhancing Code Pre-trained Models via Contrastive Learning"

        venue: ICSE

        relation: background
